problem:
Problem description
- There is a finite set of batches $$\mathcal{I}$$ and a finite set of dyeing vats $$\mathcal{J}$$ arranged in a fixed processing order.
- Each batch $$i \in \mathcal{I}$$ must be processed once in every vat $$j \in \mathcal{J}$$, and the processing stages must be completed in the same technological order for every batch.
- The processing time of batch $$i$$ in vat $$j$$ is given by the parameter $$p_{i,j}$$.
- The planning horizon is continuous time, and all scheduling decisions are made over that horizon.
- The planning goal is to minimize the completion time of the last finished batch, i.e. the overall makespan.
- Required business rules:
  - Every batch must visit all vats in the prescribed order.
  - A batch may start processing in a vat only after it has completed the previous vat.
  - Each vat can process at most one batch at a time.
  - A batch can be processed by at most one vat at a time.
  - Processing, once started on a vat, is non-preemptive.
  - All batches must be completed.
- The objective is to find a schedule that minimizes the maximum completion time across all batches.
- The relevant symbols are:
  - $$N$$: number of batches.
  - $$M$$: number of vats.
  - $$\mathcal{I}=\{1,\dots,N\}$$: set of batch indices.
  - $$\mathcal{J}=\{1,\dots,M\}$$: set of vat indices.
  - $$p_{i,j}$$: processing time of batch $$i$$ in vat $$j$$.
  - $$s_{i,j}$$: start time of batch $$i$$ in vat $$j$$.
  - $$c_{i,j}$$: completion time of batch $$i$$ in vat $$j$$.
  - $$\pi$$: processing sequence of the batches.
  - $$C_{\max}$$: completion time of the last finished batch.
- A solution is represented by:
  - an ordered sequence $$\pi$$ of the batches,
  - start times $$s_{i,j}$$ for every batch-vat pair,
  - completion times $$c_{i,j}$$ for every batch-vat pair,
  - the makespan value $$C_{\max}$$.

Input Format
- The input is a JSON-style object describing the scheduling instance.
- Required fields:
  - $$N$$: integer, the number of batches.
  - $$M$$: integer, the number of vats.
  - $$P$$: a matrix of size $$N \times M$$, where $$P_{i,j}=p_{i,j}$$ is the processing time of batch $$i$$ in vat $$j$$.
- Optional fields:
  - $$\mathcal{I}$$ and $$\mathcal{J}$$ may be omitted if indices are implied by $$N$$ and $$M$$.
- Schema:
  - $$\texttt{\{}$$
    - $$\texttt{"N"}$$: $$N$$,
    - $$\texttt{"M"}$$: $$M$$,
    - $$\texttt{"P"}$$: $$[ [p_{1,1},\dots,p_{1,M}], \dots, [p_{N,1},\dots,p_{N,M}] ]$$
  - $$\texttt{\}}$$

Output Format
- The output is a JSON-style object describing the schedule.
- Required fields:
  - $$\pi$$: the chosen batch sequence, represented as a permutation of $$\{1,\dots,N\}$$.
  - $$S$$: a matrix of size $$N \times M$$, where $$S_{i,j}=s_{i,j}$$ is the start time of batch $$i$$ in vat $$j$$.
  - $$C$$: a matrix of size $$N \times M$$, where $$C_{i,j}=c_{i,j}$$ is the completion time of batch $$i$$ in vat $$j$$.
  - $$C_{\max}$$: the makespan, equal to the final completion time of the schedule.
- Schema:
  - $$\texttt{\{}$$
    - $$\texttt{"pi"}$$: $$[\pi_1,\dots,\pi_N]$$,
    - $$\texttt{"S"}$$: $$[ [s_{1,1},\dots,s_{1,M}], \dots, [s_{N,1},\dots,s_{N,M}] ]$$,
    - $$\texttt{"C"}$$: $$[ [c_{1,1},\dots,c_{1,M}], \dots, [c_{N,1},\dots,c_{N,M}] ]$$,
    - $$\texttt{"Cmax"}$$: $$C_{\max}$$
  - $$\texttt{\}}$$

Example(s)

Input 1
{
  "N": 5,
  "M": 3,
  "P": [
    [3, 1, 1],
    [2, 1.5, 1],
    [3, 1.2, 1.3],
    [2, 2, 2],
    [2.1, 2, 3]
  ]
}

parameters.name: num_batches
parameters.description: Number of batches; defines the batch index set $\mathcal{I}=\{0,1,\dots,N-1\}$.

parameters.name: num_vats
parameters.description: Number of dyeing vats; defines the vat index set $\mathcal{J}=\{0,1,\dots,M-1\}$.

parameters.name: processing_time
parameters.description: Processing time of batch $i$ in vat $j$.

variables.name: batch_sequence
variables.description: Ordered sequence (permutation) of the batches in processing order.

variables.name: start_time
variables.description: Start time of batch $i$ in vat $j$.

variables.name: completion_time
variables.description: Completion time of batch $i$ in vat $j$.

variables.name: makespan
variables.description: Completion time of the last finished batch.

constraints.name: positive_instance_sizes
constraints.description: the number of batches and the number of vats must be positive integers

constraints.name: nonnegative_processing_times
constraints.description: processing times must be nonnegative for all batch-vat pairs

constraints.name: nonnegative_times
constraints.description: Start times, completion times, and makespan must be nonnegative.

constraints.name: permutation_sequence
constraints.description: The batch sequence variable must be a permutation of all batch indices.

constraints.name: nonpreemptive_processing
constraints.description: once a batch starts in a vat it must run continuously until completion

constraints.name: fixed_vat_order
constraints.description: each batch must visit the vats in the same prescribed technological order

constraints.name: precedence_within_batch
constraints.description: a batch may start in a vat only after it has completed the previous vat

constraints.name: single_batch_per_vat
constraints.description: each vat can process at most one batch at a time; enforced via the common batch sequence representation and non-overlap timing logic
constraints.formula: \text{No overlap of batches on any vat consistent with the common permutation }\pi

constraints.name: single_vat_per_batch
constraints.description: a batch can be processed by at most one vat at a time; this is already implied by the fixed technological order and stage-wise timing

constraints.name: all_batches_completed
constraints.description: All batches must be completed by the end of the schedule; this is enforced by the makespan definition.

constraints.name: processing_time_consistency
constraints.description: Completion times equal start times plus the fixed processing times for every batch-vat pair.

constraints.name: within_batch_vat_order
constraints.description: Each batch must start in vat j only after completing vat j-1, preserving the fixed technological order.

constraints.name: makespan_definition
constraints.description: The makespan is at least the completion time of every batch in every vat.

objectives.name: makespan_minimization
objectives.description: minimize the completion time of the last finished batch

final_objective.description: Minimize the makespan, i.e., the completion time of the last finished batch.
